checklist.name: basal ganglia or thalamic abnormality

checklist.name: medulla or cervical spinal cord atrophy or signal abnormality

quotes.text: 頭部 MRI にて延髄・頸髄の萎縮・異常信号は必発である
atrophy and/or abnormal signals of the medulla oblongata (MO) and cervical spinal cord
atrophy of the brainstem and cerebellum

checklist.why: Described as invariable in late-onset disease (tadpole appearance, eye spot sign, nodular lesions).

left_out: gait disturbance: a consequence of weakness, spasticity or ataxia, so it would overlap those items
bulbar or pseudobulbar signs as one item: split into dysphagia and dysarthria or dysphonia, which papers name directly
rigidity (筋強剛): named once in a list; less often reported
encephalopathy, malnutrition and paroxysmal deterioration (Prust Type I list): vague or overlapping with feeding and dysphagia
abnormality of the dentate nucleus hilum and midbrain signal abnormality or rim: fine imaging details, less often stated; cerebellar atrophy left out with them
ventricular garland and white matter cysts: would sit inside cerebral white matter abnormality
Rosenthal fibers: pathological hallmark used to confirm the diagnosis, seen only on biopsy or autopsy
somatic sensory dysfunction and 'other brainstem signs': only category labels in a figure legend
nystagmus and spastic ataxia: appear only in reference titles and would sit inside existing items
notes: Sources: Grossi 2024 (39420046, genetics meta-analysis with little clinical text), Yoshida 2020 (32779598, Japanese; most quotes come from its diagnostic criteria table and clinical sections, copied verbatim including the stray spaces inside words from PDF conversion) and Messing 2025 (40520824, mostly age at onset and survival). Twelve clinical items are followed by eight imaging items, because MRI findings define the subtypes and case reports routinely describe them. Judgement calls: dysphagia and dysarthria or dysphonia are separate items rather than one bulbar item; autonomic dysfunction is a composite following the criteria's own grouping, which puts sleep apnea under it; cognitive decline (loss of function) is kept apart from developmental delay (failure to gain skills). Rosenthal fibers and the dentate hilum item were the closest exclusions.
